messages:
anya: Hey — I’m opening my first non-trivial PR in the monorepo. Quick ?s about branching / commit style / reviewers so I don’t screw up the flow.
samir: Welcome! TL;DR: use the branch pattern, conventional-style commits, run the local checks, add the right reviewers. Longer below.
meera: Branching: feature branches -> feat/<ticket>-short-desc, bugfix -> fix/<ticket>-short, docs -> docs/<short>. Keep names lowercase, hyphens, max ~50 chars.
samir: Commits: we follow Conventional Commits. Example:

```
feat(auth): add oauth token refresh handler
fix(cli): handle ctrl-c during upload
chore(deps): bump protobuf -> 4.0.0
```

Squash on merge is our default, so make one logical commit per PR if you can.
anya: Got it. What about PR reviewers? who do I add for runtime code vs infra vs docs?
meera: CODEOWNERS covers most. For runtime/serving -> @eng-runtime, infra -> @eng-infra, platform -> @eng-platform. If touching cross-cutting infra, add @kevin (arch) and tag as "needs-2-reviews".
kevin: For core infra or breaking changes, we require 2 reviewers including at least one senior on the owning team. For tiny docs/typos 1 reviewer is fine. If you're unsure, add the owning team and ping #eng-architects.
samir: CI checks: unit + lint + mypy + integration smoke. Run locally: `./scripts/bootstrap && ./scripts/test-local --fast` before pushing. If CI fails, click "Re-run checks" in GH, or rebase on main and push --force-with-lease.
anya: Any recommended git commands for keeping branch tidy?
meera: Yes:
```
git fetch origin
git checkout -b feat/1234-add-thing
# work, then
git add .
git commit -m "feat(module): short summary"
# keep branch up to date
git pull --rebase origin/main
# when ready
git push --set-upstream origin feat/1234-add-thing
# if rebased
git push --force-with-lease
```
samir: PR template highlights to include in description (we have a bot that enforces these):

- Summary of change
- Jira/Issue link
- Migration notes (if any)
- How to test (local steps)
- Checklist: unit tests, integration, docs updated

Example snippet our template auto-injects:

```
### What changed
- short bullet list

### How to test
1. ./scripts/start-dev
2. curl http://localhost:8080/health

### Checklist
- [ ] unit tests
- [ ] integration smoke
- [ ] changelog/docs
```

devx-bot: Autolabeler will add labels based on files changed. Use `Draft` status for WIP PRs; mark `Ready for review` when you want lenient review flow. :robot_face:
kevin: A few house rules: small PRs (<200 LOC) get faster reviews. For large refactors, create an ADR or RFC first and split into smaller PRs. Avoid mixing formatting-only commits with feature work in the same PR.
anya: One hiccup I hit: lint failure in js package — CI showed `eslint: no-unused-vars` on generated test fixture. Best fix?
meera: If it's generated, update the generator or add a quick ignore in the file with `/* eslint-disable no-unused-vars */` and add a note. Prefer fixing generator if you can. Re-run `./scripts/lint js` locally.
samir: If CI stays flaky, comment `@devx-bot re-run` (we allow maintainers to re-run). For flaky integration tests we tag them `flaky` and skip locally.
anya: Perfect — thanks everyone, this is super helpful. I’ll open the PR as draft first and ping reviewers when ready. :pray:
meera: Welcome aboard! ping me if you want a quick pair-review before formal reviews.
kevin: +1 — happy to review once you’re ready.
